source_admission: Published values and models used by power.py and power.md; no external dataset or document is admitted to Git. The ITU-R tables and validation values the screen uses are transcribed into power.py as constants and checked there against the documents named here. 'access' records how far each source was checked on 12 October 2026: 'full text' means the document itself was read, at least the parts named; 'checked by reproduction' means equations written from the standard and confirmed by reproducing the published values named; 'via the provisioning literature search' means the entry and its reading in provisioning/sources.json, not re-read here; 'via search summary' means a web search's summary, the document not opened. Copies of the ITU documents read, with their sha256, are kept in the ignored run folder research/runs/provisioning/power/, not in the repository. Repository products are bound by hash in the product.

sources.citation: ITU-R 2022, Recommendation ITU-R P.676-13 (08/2022), Attenuation by atmospheric gases and related effects
sources.use: Annex 1 equations 1-9 (specific attenuation from 44 oxygen lines, the Debye spectrum and pressure-induced nitrogen, and 35 water-vapour lines including the 1,780 GHz pseudo-line), Tables 1 and 2 transcribed in full, and equations 13-19b for slant paths through layers 10 cm thick at the ground thickening by e^(1/100); PDF sha256 8c09b2d2c120bdae33f60c2a7abff873374d54075ce0dc71060de8a5507bbe2f

sources.citation: ITU-R Study Group 3 2024, Validation examples for Study Group 3 Earth-space propagation prediction methods, CG-3M3J-13-ValEx-Rev8.3.0
sources.use: the recommendations' own Earth values: P.676-13 gamma_o and gamma_w at 1-350 GHz for 1,013.25 hPa, 288.15 K and 7.5 g/m3 (15 of them kept as checks); the slant-path example at 28 GHz and 30 degrees through the P.835-6 mean annual global atmosphere, 0.47081173472870 dB over 922 layers, with its layer values; P.838-3 coefficients at 14.25 and 29 GHz; workbook sha256 e2d8d864c80f59752318548cdd75d818792b44574da6e41dbdc5cb722aab7546
sources.access: full text (sheets P.676-13 SpAtt, P.676-13 A_Gas_A1_2.2.1a and P.838-3 Sp.Att)

sources.citation: ITU-R 2017, Recommendation ITU-R P.835-6, Reference standard atmospheres
sources.use: the mean annual global reference atmosphere (temperature and pressure by geopotential height to 86 km and the polynomial above, water vapour 7.5 exp(-h/2) g/m3 held to a mixing ratio of 2e-6) for the Earth check of the slant-path method
sources.access: checked by reproduction: the profile reproduces the validation file's pressure, temperature and water vapour at all 922 layer mid-points to 1e-13; the recommendation itself not opened

sources.citation: ITU-R 2019, Recommendation ITU-R P.453-14, The radio refractive index: its formula and refractivity data
sources.use: N = 77.6 p_dry/T + 72 e/T + 3.75e5 e/T^2 for the refractive index in the slant paths
sources.access: checked by reproduction: the validation file's refractive index at the ground and its slant-path result are reproduced; the recommendation itself not opened

sources.citation: ITU-R 2005, Recommendation ITU-R P.838-3, Specific attenuation model for rain for use in prediction methods
sources.use: gamma_R = k R^alpha with k and alpha from equations 2-5 and Tables 1-4, checked against its Table 5 at 2-6 GHz; PDF sha256 3ab7482993e51fc63c5127a72e9e8930614e73652ac614882760817e7c1469cb

sources.citation: US DOE & NASA 1978, Satellite Power System Concept Development and Evaluation Program: Reference System Report, DOE/ER-0023
sources.use: the 2.45 GHz reference link, its rectenna at most 23 mW/cm2 (230 W/m2) at the centre and its retrodirective beam, as the domain synthesis reads them; the tau of 2.04 comes from the provisioning population product

sources.citation: Rodenbeck, Jaffe, Strassner, Hausgen, McSpadden et al. 2021, IEEE Journal of Microwaves 1, 229-259
sources.use: beam collection set by the geometric mean of the apertures over wavelength times distance (tau)
sources.access: via the provisioning population sources (full text there)
